chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-'Alawi, who said:

Abu Muhammad (عليه السلام) was imprisoned with 'Ali ibn Narmash, and he was the most hostile of the people and the harshest of them against the family of Abu Talib. And it was said to him, "Do this to him and do that," but he did not remain with him except for a day until he placed his cheeks before him in submission, and he would not raise his gaze toward him out of reverence and magnification. Then he came out from his presence while he had become the most perceptive of the people regarding him and the best of them in speech about him.

key_terms.آلِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ: the family of Abu Talib, referring to the Prophet’s family line and the Imams (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: a kunyah referring here to Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام)
key_terms.أَنْصَبُ: the most hostile toward the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام)
key_terms.إِعْظَامًا: out of exaltation and great respect
key_terms.قَوْلًا: speech or manner of speaking regarding someone

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Hasan al-'Askari (عليه السلام) affect the attitude of his hostile prison guard?
ai.summary: This report describes how the spiritual dignity of Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn 'Ali (عليه السلام) transformed even a deeply hostile jailer in a very short time. It highlights the Imam’s awe-inspiring presence and serves as a biographical testimony to his rank and the effect of his character upon opponents.
